question.problem:
The disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ of events ${A}_{1},{A}_{2},{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P({A}_{2}|B)$ given the following probabilities:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P(B|{A}_{1})=0.75, &  \\  & P(B|{A}_{2})=0.15, & P({A}_{2})=0.3 \\  & P(B|{A}_{3})=0.8, & P({A}_{3})=0.6\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If the disjoint union ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔…⊔{A}_{n}$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

$$
P({A}_{k}|B)=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{P(B)}=\frac{P(B|{A}_{k})P({A}_{k})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})}
$$

where $k=1,2,…,n.$

In our case, $n=3,$ and ${A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2}⊔{A}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

$$
P({A}_{1})+P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})=1.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{1}) & =1-(P({A}_{2})+P({A}_{3})) \\  & =1-(0.3+0.6) \\  & =0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}_{2}|B) & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})}{{\sum }_{i=1}^{3}P(B|{A}_{i})P({A}_{i})} \\  & =\frac{P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})}{P(B|{A}_{1})P({A}_{1})+P(B|{A}_{2})P({A}_{2})+P(B|{A}_{3})P({A}_{3})} \\  & =\frac{(0.15)(0.3)}{(0.75)(0.1)+(0.15)(0.3)+(0.8)(0.6)} \\  & =\frac{0.045}{0.6} \\  & =0.075.\end{aligned}
$$
